Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic stacks.
The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is locally quasi-finite,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> is quasi-DM and for any morphism <MATH_0004> with <MATH_0005>
an algebraic space and any locally quasi-finite morphism
<MATH_0006> where <MATH_0007> is an algebraic space
the morphism <MATH_0008> is locally quasi-finite,
<STRUCT_0004> for any morphism <MATH_0009> from an algebraic space <MATH_0010>
there exists a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented, and locally
quasi-finite morphism <MATH_0011> where
<MATH_0012> is an algebraic space such that <MATH_0013> is locally quasi-finite,
<STRUCT_0005> there exists algebraic spaces <MATH_0014>, <MATH_0015>, a surjective, flat,
and locally of finite presentation morphism <MATH_0016>,
and a morphism <MATH_0017> which
is surjective, flat, locally of finite presentation, and
locally quasi-finite such that <MATH_0018> is locally quasi-finite.
<STRUCT_0006>

Assume (1). Then <MATH_0001> is quasi-DM by assumption. Let
<MATH_0002> and <MATH_0003>
be as in (2). By
Lemma <REF_0001>
the composition <MATH_0004> is
locally quasi-finite. Thus (1) implies (2).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume (2). Let <MATH_0005> be as in (3). By
Lemma <REF_0002>
we can find an algebraic space <MATH_0006> and a surjective, flat, locally
finitely presented, locally quasi-finite morphism
<MATH_0007>. By (2) the composition
<MATH_0008> is locally quasi-finite. Thus (2) implies (3).

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
It is immediate that (3) implies (4).

<STRUCT_0005><STRUCT_0006>
Assume (4). We will prove (1) holds, which finishes the proof. By
Lemma <REF_0003>
we see that <MATH_0009> is quasi-DM. To prove that <MATH_0010> is locally of finite type
it suffices to prove that <MATH_0011> is
locally of finite type, see
Lemma <REF_0004>.
Then it suffices to check that <MATH_0012> precomposed with
<MATH_0013> is locally of finite type, see
Lemma <REF_0005>.
Since <MATH_0014> was assumed to be locally quasi-finite
this holds, hence <MATH_0015> is locally of finite type.
Finally, let <MATH_0016> be a field and let <MATH_0017>
be a morphism. Then <MATH_0018> is
a nonempty algebraic space which is locally of finite presentation
over <MATH_0019>. Hence we can find a finite extension <MATH_0020> and
a morphism <MATH_0021> such that
<MATH_0022>
commutes (details omitted). Then <MATH_0023>
is representable (by schemes), surjective, and finite locally free. In
particular <MATH_0024> is surjective and open.
Thus it suffices to prove that <MATH_0025> is discrete. Since
<MATH_0026>
we see that <MATH_0027> is
surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation (as a base change
of <MATH_0028>). Hence
<MATH_0029> is surjective and
open. Thus it suffices to show that <MATH_0030> is
discrete. This follows from the fact that <MATH_0031> is locally
quasi-finite (either by our definition above or from the original definition
for morphisms of algebraic spaces, via
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0006>).
